b_mass = {\"v1\": 0.0, \"v2\": 0.0, \"v3\": 0.0}\n    for e in chosen:\n        b = min(b_mass, key=lambda k: (b_mass[k], len(buckets[k])))\n        buckets[b].append(e)\n        b_mass[b] += Furthermore, the threshold `top_p >= 0.985` is clearly suboptimal, and I am calculating the Bayes-optimal accusation threshold. I'm assessing the trade-off between immediate accusation versus waiting, and the impacts on the mean score.\n\n\n**Optimizing Accusation Thresholds**\n\nI've been calculating optimal accusation thresholds, and have worked out that immediately accusing at $p \\ge 0.96$ is more optimal, with waiting suggested at lower probabilities. The reasoning involves evaluating the expected values, the uncertainty costs, and the risk of losing.\n\n\\n\\n\nI also looked into the expected value of acting immediately versus waiting. At a value of $V=0.75$, I've calculated that a probability of $p=0.943$ yields equal expected score. I am now checking those calculations. I'm adding targeted canaries on Days 1 and 2 to see if it speeds up the investigation. By focusing on people who already received documents, I believe it will improve the mean time to discovery. 3},\n]\nEMP_MAP = {e[\"id\"]: e for e in EMPLOYEES}\nDECOY = \"e23\"\n\ndef compute_posterior(state):\n    docs = {d[\"doc_id\"]: d for d in state[\"documents\"]}\n    leaks = state[\"leaks\"]          # list of {\"surfaced_day\", \"doc_id\", \"variant\"(optional)}\n    logs = state[\"logs\"]            # list of {\"day\", \"employee\", \"doc_id\", \"after_hours\"}\n    interviews = state[\"interviews\"] # list of {\"day\", \"employee\", \"topic\", \"evasive\"}\n    closed_days = state[\"closed_days\"]\n\n    # Track log-likelihood per employee\n    log_p = {}\n    for e in EMPLOYEES:\n        eid = e[\"id\"]\n        if eid == DECOY:\n            log_p[eid] = -1e18\n        else:\n            log_p[eid] = 0.0\n\n    # 1. Hard recipient membership + canary variant accuracy (0.95 vs 0.05/(M-1))\n    for lk in leaks:\n        doc = docs[lk[\"doc_id\"]]\n        recs = set(doc[\"recipients\"])\n        for eid in list(log_p.keys()):\n            if log_p[eid] <= -1e15:\n                continue\n            if eid not in recs:\n                log_p[eid] = -1e18\n            elif doc.get(\"is_canary\"):\n                variants = doc[\"variants\"] # variant -> list of emp ids\n                M = len(variants)\n                shown_v = lk.get(\"variant\")\n                if shown_v is not None and M >= 2:\n                    emp_v = None\n                    for v_label, elist in variants.items():\n                        if eid in elist:\n                            emp_v = v_label\n                            break\n                    if emp_v == shown_v:\n                        log_p[eid] += math.log(0.95)\n                    else:\n                        log_p[eid] += math.log(0.05 / (M - 1))\n\n    # 2. Access logs likelihood across closed days\n    # For each closed day d, determine which employees held >= 1 document on day d\n    # Innocent non-decoy holding docs:\n    #   daytime ~ Pois(0.9)\n    #   after_hours ~ Pois(0.1 + framing_colleague_rate)\n    #   Baseline framing colleague rate = 2.0 * 0.5 / 38 = 1/38.\n    #   (If a DSL rule also frames random colleague, rate could be 2/38; if decoy or none, 1/38. We check sensitivity to both!)\n    framing_col_rate = state.get(\"framing_col_rate\", 1.0 / 38.0)\n    for d in range(1, closed_days + 1):\n        held = set()\n        for doc in docs.values():\n            if doc[\"day\"] <= d:\n                held.update(doc[\"recipients\"])\n        # Count daytime and after_hours per employee on day d\n        dt_cnt = {e[\"id\"]: 0 for e in EMPLOYEES}\n        ah_cnt = {e[\"id\"]: 0 for e in EMPLOYEES}\n        for lg in logs:\n            if lg[\"day\"] == d:\n                if lg[\"after_hours\"]:\n                    ah_cnt[lg[\"employee\"]] += 1\n                else:\n                    dt_cnt[lg[\"employee\"]] += 1\n        for eid in list(log_p.keys()):\n            if log_p[eid] <= -1e15:\n                continue\n            if eid in held:\n                # Ratio P(dt, ah | eid is mole) / P(dt, ah | eid is innocent)\n                # Mole: dt ~ Pois(0.7), ah ~ Pois(0.3)\n                # Inn:  dt ~ Pois(0.9), ah ~ Pois(0.1 + framing_col_rate)\n                lam_ah_inn = 0.1 + framing_col_rate\n                dt = dt_cnt[eid]\n                ah = ah_cnt[eid]\n                # log LR = -(0.7 + 0.3) + (0.9 + lam_ah_inn) + dt*log(0.7/0.9) + ah*log(0.3/lam_ah_inn)\n                llr = (-1.0 + 0.9 + lam_ah_inn) + dt * math.log(0.7 / 0.9) + ah * math.log(0.3 / lam_ah_inn)\n                log_p[eid] += llr\n\n    # 3. Interviews (deduplicated by (day, employee, topic))\n    seen_int = set()\n    for iv in interviews:\n        key = (iv[\"day\"], iv[\"employee\"], iv[\"topic\"])\n        if key in seen_int:\n            continue\n        seen_int.add(key)\n        eid = iv[\"employee\"]\n        if log_p[eid] <= -1e15:\n            continue\n        if iv[\"evasive\"]:\n            log_p[eid] += math.log(0.24 / 0.20)\n        else:\n            log_p[eid] += math.log(0.76 / 0.80)\n\n    # Normalize\n    valid = [v for v in log_p.values() if v > -1e15]\n    mx = max(valid)\n    probs = {}\n    tot = 0.0\n    for eid, lp in log_p.items():\n        if lp <= -1e15:\n            probs[eid] = 0.0\n        else:\n            w = math.exp(lp - mx)\n            probs[eid] = w\n            tot += w\n    for eid in probs:\n        probs[eid] /= tot\n    return probs\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    with open(\"/tmp/opencode/state.json\") as f:\n        st = json.load(f)\n    probs = compute_posterior(st)\n    st_dsl_frame = dict(st, framing_col_rate=2.0 / 38.0)\n    probs2 = compute_posterior(st_dsl_frame)\n    ranked = sorted(EMPLOYEES, key=lambda e: probs[e[\"id\"]], reverse=True)\n    print(\"Top suspects (baseline framing vs +DSL random framing):\")\n    for e in ranked:\n        eid = e[\"id\"]\n        if probs[eid] > 0:\n            print(f\"  {eid} ({e['dept']:11s} cl={e['clearance']}): P={probs[eid]:.4f}  (P_dsl2={probs2[eid]:.4f})\")\n","filePath":"/tmp/opencode/tracker.py"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/tmp/opencode/tracker.py","exists":false,"truncated":false},"title":"tmp/opencode/tracker.py","time":{"start":1794701517913,"end":1794701517919}},"metadata":{"google":{"thoughtSignature":""}},"id":"prt_1dc8be455001Z74Q5z2inDzT2M","sessionID":"ses_e237f0c38ffelF1IAZslS8mAQz","messageID":"msg_1dc8aa399001Dtv6926D2pcnv1"}}

Restricting the mole (e13 in my thought experiment) on Days 11, 12, and 13 prevents any leaks by e13 on Days 13, 14, and 15, as no documents will be available to the mole on those days! This potentially streamlines the entire solution, and simplifies the benchmark strategy! The key is the timing and impact of `advance_day`. It turns out regular documents are published *before* a restricted mole, in this case, `e13`, receives anything! So, if `e13` is restricted when the day advances, it *won't* receive those new documents. Then, with a simple call to `unrestrict_access(\"e13\")` and by planting a canary `c`, I can guarantee `c` is the *only* document `e13` has access to that day. The benchmark solution is now much clearer! I must now verify this entire mechanic, detail by detail, against every rule.\n\n\n**Simplifying Mole Identification**\n\nI've had a profound realization! Restricting employee `e13` on Day 10 immediately proves its innocence if documents leak on Day 11, because `e13` doesn't receive those documents.
